analysis.title: Textron Inc. (TXT): 3Q26 earnings callback; Neutral
key_insights: GS hosted a group investor meeting with Textron CFO Dave Rosenberg after the 3Q26 earnings update. Topics were aviation operational improvements, MV-75 funding mechanics, Systems growth and cash flow. GS keeps a Neutral rating.

Aviation demand is strong across the board, with backlog now extending over about 3 years for newer aircraft variants. King Air and SkyCourier are not an insignificant portion of the $8.0bn aviation backlog.

Textron has historically seen 20-25% incremental aviation margins. It is investing in tooling, labor and second sources to get back to that range, and expects the P&L to improve over the next twelve months, though quarter-to-quarter results may be lumpy.
Management believes it can reach the aviation margin target through efficiency gains from reallocating existing Textron resources.

The US Army received congressional approval for a $350mn ATR (above threshold reprogramming) tied to the MV-75 program. About $300mn was obligated to the program in contract modifications to cover Textron's investments.
The $350mn requested in 2Q was an estimate made before actuals arrived, and the $300mn covers actual accrued expenses. The ATR still has funds remaining for future or additional expenses.
Textron is now in a normal billing and invoice cycle for MV-75, and its revised cash flow guidance includes the expected payments.

Textron raised full-year 2026 manufacturing cash flow guidance by $100mn. The largest driver was a capex reduction of about $100mn, as spend is re-aligned to the funding environment under the continuing resolution (CR).
Capex is expected to stay elevated for multiple years. Textron has historically put the majority of free cash toward share repurchases and says that remains the plan.
GS's 12-month price target is $94, based on 9.0x EV/EBITDA on 2027E EBITDA. Key risks are business jet demand, new program execution and DoD spending.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $94 target (from $93 on 29-Jul-26), about 6.2% above the $88.53 close on 2 Nov 2026. The target uses 9.0x EV/EBITDA on 2027E EBITDA.

earnings_insights: TXT 3Q26 earnings were reported before this 2 Nov 2026 callback. The note gives no 3Q26 EPS or revenue print.
GS estimates (not reported): 2026E EPS $6.63, 2027E EPS $7.22 and 2028E EPS $8.37, against 2025 reported EPS of $6.10.
GS quarterly EPS: 9/26 $1.76 and 12/26E $1.81. Estimates are 3/27E $1.48 and 6/27E $1.78. The 9/26 figure is shown without a reported or adjusted qualifier.
GS estimates for 2026E revenue are $15,560.4mn and for EBITDA $1,865.0mn, against 2025 revenue of $14,799.0mn and EBITDA of $1,764.0mn. 2027E estimates are revenue $16,573.4mn and EBITDA $2,006.1mn.
Textron raised full-year 2026 manufacturing cash flow guidance by $100mn, mostly from about $100mn lower capex.
risk_factors: DoD spending, including the funding environment under the continuing resolution.
